items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: Before then our authorities were John Hammond and Martin Williams and Charles Edward Smith and so on, all of whom were good, responsible authors

ctx.x: There’s been a few books out focused on white musicians’ contributions to jazz including our friend Randy Sandke. And I’m going to take a stab at this question — do you think black authors and researchers write differently about blues and jazz than white authors and researchers do? © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Well I could probably say that each author writes with his own set of principles an emphases and so on, and that the division isn’t necessarily racial, it’s just, you know the kind of intellectual freedom we allow ourselves among historians and critics and so on. But certainly somebody years and years ago writing about jazz was assumed to be white. We didn’t have black authorities starting to get involved with the music and writing about it seriously and in some depth in creating books. That didn’t really start…
